shouldFix.title: A harness specification with no pass property, no fail conditions, and none of the execution semantics its parent already supplied
shouldFix.location: absent keys: passProperty, failsIf, matrix, retainedEvidence, and any executes* field; namedCorpusClasses members carry no passProperty either
shouldFix.finding: The artifact's purpose is 'Close leftover-design of the unauthored G31 harness specification by stating exact-byte intent for execution of the eleven already-authored D-130 classes.' It states what the fixtures are and what each one's expected fate is, and then stops. It never says what it means for G31 to pass, or what makes it fail. I checked whether that is the document class's shape and it is not. The four full harness specifications in this corpus — G07 v3, G09 v3, G15 v7, G16 v2 — each carry a top-level passProperty and a failsIf list, alongside matrix and retainedEvidence. I then checked whether the '.preview' suffix licenses a thinner artifact, since G26 v1 is the other preview harness and does lack top-level passProperty and failsIf; it does not license this, because G26 v1 carries retainedEvidence whose every member states its own exactByteIntent and its own passProperty. So both shapes in this corpus state pass conditions, one at the top level and one per evidence member. This subject states none at either level: its namedCorpusClasses members carry id, memberVerbatim, primary, also, fixtureBytes and executedHere, and no passProperty or exactByteIntent.
shouldFix.whatMakesItPointed: The material was not unavailable — it was in the parent this artifact pins and quotes four other fields from. Naming v1's gate.executesIfRecorded reads 'The eleven D-130 classes only, in the verbatim order namedElevenClassesVerbatim. Each class primary must reproduce its D-130 pinned digest and expected fate. Also-bytes listed at D-130 remain also-bytes, not a twelfth class.' Its proposed evidenceCell adds 'each class primary reproduces its D-130 pinned digest and expected fate'. I searched the subject for that language and it is absent: 'must reproduce its D-130 pinned digest', 'reproduces its D-130 pinned digest', 'in the verbatim order' and 'remain also-bytes, not a twelfth class' all return zero. The specification carries claimVerbatim, waiverRuleVerbatim, proposedHarnessCellVerbatim and notATwelfthClass from that parent, and leaves behind precisely the field that says what running the harness proves.
shouldFix.concreteConsequences: Two, both of which every sibling closes. First, nothing in this specification requires a runner to verify the fixture digests at execution time. It pins seventeen digests — I confirmed all seventeen reproduce today — but pinning a digest in a specification is not the same as making reproduction a pass condition, and the parent's 'must reproduce' is the sentence that would have done that. Second, there is no vacuous-pass guard. G07 v3, G09 v3, G15 v7 and G16 v2 each carry failsIf entries that make a missing or empty measurement a fail rather than a pass; here nothing states that a run executing zero of the eleven classes, or producing no report, fails. The waiverRuleVerbatim 'pass all; no waiver for silent accept of a refuse class' does real work and is the closest thing present, but it is a waiver rule quoted from the parent's proposed file-08 cell, and it presupposes a pass condition rather than supplying one.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: Nothing in the artifact is false, no row moves, required-now is untouched, the artifact binds NOTHING and is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, and the missing semantics are recoverable from the parent it pins by digest. The defect is incompleteness of the deliverable against its own stated purpose, not an error in what it does say.
shouldFix.whatWouldRepairIt: State a passProperty — at minimum that each of the eleven class primaries reproduces its D-130 pinned digest and produces its expected fate, all eleven pass, and also-bytes are not scored as a twelfth class — and a failsIf list that at least makes a missing or partial run a fail rather than a pass. The parent supplies the first half almost word for word.
shouldFix.notAssertedByThisFinding: I do not author the pass property, propose failsIf entries beyond naming the vacuous-pass gap that the siblings close, execute any class, or claim the eleven fixtures would fail. The finding is that the specification does not say what passing is.

independence.priorParticipation: The sharpest in this sequence, and it needs stating first rather than last. This artifact's parentReview pins my own verdict from the immediately preceding review cycle, by digest, and describes the rule it is following as CLAUDE-G03-V1-SF1 — a SHOULD-FIX I raised earlier in this session about occupancy files pinning their parent review. It also pins the D-056 turn-2 draft, which is the advisory I raised against its parent one cycle ago. So the subject is visibly built to satisfy me, and it is the situation in which a reviewer is most likely to confirm rather than refute. Three things I did about it. First, I verified my own pinned verdict as a citation like any other — the digest reproduces and the ACCEPT 0/0 standing it is given is accurate — rather than waving it through because I wrote it. Second, I deliberately looked for defects in territory neither of my prior items touched, which is where the finding came from: the pass property and fail conditions are unrelated to parentReview pinning or D-056 pinning. Third, I graded the finding against the corpus's own document-class shape by comparing five sibling harness specifications, including checking whether the preview suffix licensed the thinner form, so the standard applied is the corpus's rather than mine. What I cannot self-certify is whether a reviewer with no stake in the two landed items would have pressed harder elsewhere; the coordinator should weigh that.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Twenty-five attacks run, one landed. Custody holds: subject 3202bdd5 at 0444, 18809 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778; live required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified with DR-G31 occurring zero times in either, which confirms this file existing is not the three-limb recording. All nine cited digests reproduce and recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head. The measurable work in this artifact is excellent and I want that on the record before the finding. Every one of the seventeen pinned fixture files — eleven primaries and six also-bytes, one of them in fixtures/dr-103.v4/ — was hashed from disk and all seventeen reproduce. The eleven classes match the D-130 authoredCatalog in order and then field by field: id, memberVerbatim, primary id, path, digest and expected fate, the also arrays and their contents, and the parent-cycle note, with zero mismatches. All four verbatim fields equal their parent by ==. The non-refusal fates are carried intact rather than normalised. executedHere is false everywhere and no byte is re-authored. I also tested two structural objections and both failed: authoring a specification for a gate absent from file 08 is inside D-056 clause 5, whose grant is not conditioned on the gate having been recorded, and the 'already-named' phrasing is qualified in the same sentence and twice more, so the footing is disclosed rather than traded on. The finding is what the specification does not say. Its purpose is to close leftover-design of the unauthored G31 harness specification, and it states no pass property and no fail conditions. I checked whether that is the document class's shape and it is not: G07 v3, G09 v3, G15 v7 and G16 v2 each carry a top-level passProperty and failsIf, and when I checked whether the preview suffix licenses a thinner artifact — G26 v1 being the other preview harness — it does not, because G26 v1 states a passProperty on every retainedEvidence member. This subject states none at either level. What makes it pointed is that the material was in the parent it pins and quotes four other fields from: naming v1's executesIfRecorded says the eleven run in the verbatim order, that each class primary must reproduce its D-130 pinned digest and expected fate, and that also-bytes remain also-bytes. I searched for that language here and all of it returns zero. Two concrete consequences follow, both closed by every sibling. Nothing requires a runner to verify the fixture digests at execution time — pinning seventeen digests is not the same as making reproduction a pass condition, and 'must reproduce' is the sentence that would have done it. And there is no vacuous-pass guard, so nothing says a run executing zero classes fails rather than passes. It is a SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker because nothing is false, no row moves, the artifact binds NOTHING, and the missing semantics sit in a parent it already pins; the repair is largely a matter of carrying one more field forward. One disclosure the coordinator should weigh heavily. This artifact's parentReview pins my own verdict from the immediately preceding cycle and names CLAUDE-G03-V1-SF1 as the rule it follows, and it pins the D-056 draft that was my advisory against its parent one cycle ago — so it is visibly built to satisfy me, which is when a reviewer most easily confirms instead of refutes. I verified my own verdict as a citation like any other, went looking in territory neither of my prior items touched, and graded the finding against five sibling specifications so the standard is the corpus's rather than mine. Whether a reviewer without that stake would have pressed harder elsewhere is not something I can self-certify.
